content: The Fellows Workbook includes a comprehensive list of projects, each with specific objectives and guidelines. These projects include the Board Review Project, the Crowd Diagnosis Project (also known as Operation Zebra or Zebra Med), the Critical Pathways Project, the Guidelines Project, the Microchapters Project, the New Pages Project, the Prevalence Project, the Resident Survival Guide Project, WikiDoc in Other Languages, and WikiPatient. For the Crowd Diagnosis Project, also referred to as Operation Zebra or Zebra Med, there are specific resources and links provided to guide the work. These include: 1. A link to high-priority signs and symptoms that should be addressed first. 2. A link explaining how to arrange or create a topic in a structurally organized manner. This page serves as the framework for microchapters and includes standardized language to ensure uniformity across the textbook. Writers are instructed to follow these guidelines when creating their pages. Individual links are provided for specific microchapter language. 3. A link to general guidelines for creating chapters and microchapters. This page outlines the goals and appropriate content for each microchapter. 4. A link to a checklist for the Causes page. The plan for the Differential Diagnosis Project involves identifying all possible causes of a symptom or disease and systematically categorizing them into three groups: most common causes, causes by organ systems, and causes in alphabetical order. Detailed instructions for this project can be found on the Differential Diagnosis Project page. Once a symptom or disease is completed, it must be listed on the Completed Signs and Symptoms page to prevent duplication of work by other research fellows. A secondary task involves ensuring that all Causes listed on the page are hyperlinked (indicated by blue text). This means that internal links must exist for all causes. Each cause should be reviewed to confirm that its corresponding page is structured according to the established guidelines. If not, the page should be reorganized to align with the Microchapter Template and Guidelines Template. Feedback from CMG (Content Management Group) can be collected in a designated area where all error messages are compiled. This feedback is essential for improving the quality and accuracy of the content.
